analysis.recent_context: Big compounding day on Saturday 2026-07-04. Chris opened with RAM-pressure triage at 10:01 SGT — 143 messages of investigation showed 6.8 GB used on a 7.8 GB box with zero swap. Root cause was a 4-day-old manually-started Xtigervnc + XFCE + noVNC stack eating ~1.5 GB idle plus uncapped gateway/dashboard RSS. The fix shipped Tier 1 (gateway + linkedin-mcp memory caps, journal vacuum, 2 GB swap, searxng-redis crash-loop diagnosis) plus a brand-new vnc-stack-on-demand skill that puts VNC behind systemd + an idle-killer cron (tears down after 10 min idle). Net: 3.2 GB used / 4.6 GB available / 2 GB swap. Then Chris opened a 122-message follow-up on the Payntra ledger from yesterday, asked for a per-row delete feature, and we shipped it end-to-end (DELETE route with ownership JOIN, optimistic UI, inline confirm UX, 5 live round-trip tests against payntra.terrybot.top, 45/45 server tests, gzipped bundle 65.85 KB). Two major features in one day: VPS is no longer RAM-stressed, and Payntra's first real iteration is shipping. The Council audio is now stale across 6 morning briefs and the gateway echo-suppression patch has been 'approved' for a week without landing — both starting to feel more like 'will it ever' than 'not yet'.

non_negotiable.title: Pick the next Payntra iteration (or next web app) before EOD Saturday
non_negotiable.reason: Payntra is the first real project on the new pipeline. It's live and stable. But the natural momentum question is: what's the next thing? This weekend is the moment to choose, not next week. The VPS pipeline is fresh in muscle memory, Payntra's commit history shows the exact pattern to follow (push → webhook → redeploy), and the vnc-stack-on-demand infrastructure means cookie-extraction for any social-media component is now cheap. Whatever gets picked today gets iterated on Sunday and Monday. Whatever doesn't get picked today sits on the back burner for another week.
